renders._yaml:
- component: figure
  id: sample_funnel
  title: Samples at each filtering step
  description: |-
    Each bar adds up the samples of every downloaded dataset at one step of the pipeline, split by the platform that measured them. It answers how many samples survive from download to the merged matrix.
    How to read: bars should shrink only a little from one step to the next. A large drop after the gene ID mapping means many datasets could not be mapped, and a drop after a filter means many samples were mostly zeros or mostly missing. Filter by step to see which datasets lose most.
    Lines and annotations: none are drawn. The pipeline rejects a sample whose share of zeros or missing values is above 0.9 by default (max_zero_ratio and max_null_ratio), and the run may have changed them.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/stableexpression/blob/1.1.0/nextflow_schema.json
  visu_type: histogram
  dict_kwargs:
    x: step
    y: samples
    color: platform
    histfunc: sum
    labels:
      step: Step
      samples: Samples
      platform: Platform

- component: figure
  id: samples_lost
  title: Samples lost at each step
  description: |-
    Each bar adds up the samples lost at one step, split by the final outcome of their dataset. It answers where in the pipeline samples are removed and which kind of dataset loses them.
    How to read: losses coloured as a dataset that was never merged are expected, since such a dataset loses everything at the step that stopped it. Losses in merged datasets are partial filtering and are the ones to check against the zero and missing-value filters.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/stableexpression/blob/1.1.0/docs/output.md
  visu_type: histogram
  dict_kwargs:
    x: step
    y: samples_lost
    color: outcome
    histfunc: sum
    labels:
      step: Step
      samples_lost: Samples lost
      outcome: Dataset outcome

- component: interactive
  title: Pipeline step
  description: Keeps only the rows of the chosen steps, so the figures and the table show one stage of the
    funnel at a time.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: step

- component: table
  title: Samples per dataset and step
  description: |-
    Each row is one dataset at one pipeline step, with its platform, final outcome, the samples it holds and the samples lost there. It answers which datasets lose samples and at which step.
    How to read: sort by samples lost to find the datasets that shrink most, then check their outcome and platform before trusting them.

- component: card
  id: dataset_attrition
  title: Datasets through the pipeline
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of datasets the run downloaded, and the bars show how many were mapped to Ensembl genes and how many reached the merged matrix. It answers how many of the public datasets end up usable.
    How to read: a large gap between downloaded and mapped means many gene ID schemes could not be translated, and a gap between mapped and merged means the sample filters or the rare-gene filter removed whole datasets. Open the outcome ring to see the reason for each.
  column: downloaded
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: attrition
  attrition_cols:
  - id_mapped
  - merged
  caption: datasets, at each step
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: sample_attrition
  title: Samples through the pipeline
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of downloaded samples, and the bars show how many remain after the ID mapping, the zero filter and the missing-value filter. It answers how much of the downloaded data the merged matrix keeps.
    How to read: a small loss at the zero and missing-value filters is normal. A large loss points to datasets with many empty measurements, so check the per-dataset table.
    Lines and annotations: the filters reject samples with more than 0.9 zeros or 0.9 missing values by default (max_zero_ratio and max_null_ratio), unless the run changed them.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/stableexpression/blob/1.1.0/nextflow_schema.json
  column: samples_downloaded
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: attrition
  attrition_cols:
  - samples_id_mapped
  - samples_after_zero_filter
  - samples_kept
  caption: samples, at each step

- component: card
  id: dataset_outcomes
  title: Dataset outcomes
  description: |-
    Each unit is one downloaded dataset and the ring splits them by what happened to it: merged, no gene mapped, only rare genes, or all samples filtered out. It answers why datasets drop out.
    How to read: a ring mostly merged is the healthy case. A large share with no gene mapped means the dataset's gene IDs are not covered by the mapping service, which is a limit of the source and not of the data.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/stableexpression/blob/1.1.0/docs/output.md
  column: samples_kept
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: outcome
  caption: datasets, by outcome

- component: card
  id: mapped_share_card
  title: Gene IDs mapped
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median share of gene IDs a dataset had that mapped to an Ensembl gene, and the histogram shows the share of each dataset. It answers how well the source gene IDs translate.
    How to read: a distribution piled near one is healthy. A low tail means datasets whose probes or transcript IDs are poorly annotated, and they add little to the merged matrix.
  column: mapped_share
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: share mapped, per dataset

- component: figure
  id: samples_per_dataset
  title: Samples kept per dataset
  description: |-
    Each bar counts datasets that kept a given number of samples in the merged matrix, split by platform. It answers how the cohort is spread over datasets.
    How to read: a few very large datasets next to many small ones mean the stability scores lean on those large datasets. A bar at zero lists datasets that did not reach the merged matrix.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median number of samples kept per dataset of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of nf-core/stableexpression.
  visu_type: histogram
  dict_kwargs:
    x: samples_kept
    color: platform
    labels:
      samples_kept: Samples kept
      platform: Platform
  reference_lines:
  - axis: x
    stat: median
    column: samples_kept

- component: figure
  id: missing_by_design
  title: Missing values by array design
  description: |-
    Each point is a dataset: the median share of missing values over its samples, against the array design that measured it. It answers whether a design leaves many genes unmeasured.
    How to read: points near zero are complete datasets. A design with every point high leaves many genes unmeasured, and those genes are scored on fewer datasets. Compare the platforms by colour.
    Lines and annotations: none are drawn. The pipeline's own limit is a missing share of 0.9 per sample (max_null_ratio), a run parameter.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/stableexpression/blob/1.1.0/nextflow_schema.json
  visu_type: strip
  dict_kwargs:
    x: design
    y: missing_share
    color: platform
    labels:
      design: Array design
      missing_share: Share of missing values
      platform: Platform

- component: interactive
  title: Dataset outcome
  description: Keeps only datasets with the chosen outcome, for example the merged ones, so the tiles describe
    what reached the analysis.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: outcome

- component: interactive
  title: Platform
  description: Keeps only datasets measured on the chosen platform, RNA-seq or microarray.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: platform

- component: table
  id: dataset_table
  title: Downloaded datasets table
  description: |-
    Each row is a downloaded dataset with its platform, gene ID mapping counts, the samples each filter rejected, its outcome and the reason it failed when it did. It answers what happened to each dataset and lets a row selection open its record.
    How to read: sort by outcome to group the failures, then read the failure reason and the mapping note to see whether the cause is the dataset or the mapping service.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: dataset

- component: advanced_viz
  id: dataset_record
  title: Dataset record
  description: |-
    One card per dataset, listing every field of its summary row. It answers what is known about the dataset picked in the table.
    How to read: select a row in the table to load its record, then check the mapping note and the samples rejected at each filter.
  kind: record_card
  roles:
    id: dataset
    title: accession

- component: advanced_viz
  id: measure_agreement
  title: Normfinder against geNorm rank
  description: |-
    Each point is a candidate gene: its rank by Normfinder on the horizontal axis and its rank by geNorm M on the vertical axis, within its expression section, coloured by section. It answers whether two independent stability methods pick the same genes.
    How to read: points near the diagonal are genes both methods rank alike, and those at the lower left are stable by both accounts. A gene far from the diagonal is good by one method only, so check its distribution before using it as a reference.
    Lines and annotations: the diagonal is y = x, where both methods give the same rank. It is a reference of the plot and not a cut-off.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15289330/ and https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12184808/
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Normfinder rank within section
    y_title: geNorm rank within section
    reference_line: diagonal
    reference_label: Same rank in both methods
    top_n_labels: 8
  roles:
    x: normfinder_rank
    y: genorm_rank
    label: gene_name
    color: section

- component: advanced_viz
  id: candidate_record
  title: Candidate gene record
  description: |-
    One card per candidate gene, listing its stability score, rank, the four measures behind it and its expression level. It answers how a single gene scored.
    How to read: select a row in the table to load a gene, then compare its measures with the section it belongs to.
  kind: record_card
  roles:
    id: gene_id
    title: gene_name

- component: card
  id: candidate_count
  title: Candidate genes
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of candidate genes that were scored, and the bar splits them by expression level. It answers how many candidates each part of the expression range contributes.
    How to read: candidates are shortlisted per section by their coefficient of variation, so every section should contribute. A level with very few candidates means that part of the range has little stable signal.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/stableexpression/blob/1.1.0/README.md
  column: gene_id
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: expression_level
  caption: candidates, by expression level
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: best_score
  title: Best stability score
  description: |-
    The hero number is the lowest stability score, the most stable candidate, and the box shows the quartiles of all scores. It answers how stable the best gene is and how the rest compare.
    How to read: lower is more stable. A best score far below the median means a clear standout, and a tight box means most candidates are alike. The score is relative to this run and has no absolute cut-off.
    Lines and annotations: none are drawn. The pipeline publishes no cut-off for the stability score.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/stableexpression/blob/1.1.0/README.md
  column: stability_score
  aggregation: min
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: scores, with their spread
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: candidate_measured
  title: Share of samples measuring a gene
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median share of samples in which a candidate gene was measured, and the histogram shows its spread over candidates. It answers how complete the evidence behind each score is.
    How to read: a gene measured in few samples is scored on little evidence and carries a missing-value penalty. Prefer candidates with a high share.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/stableexpression/blob/1.1.0/nextflow_schema.json
  column: measured_share
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: share measured, per candidate

- component: figure
  id: score_by_section
  title: Stability score by section
  description: |-
    Each box is an expression section and summarises the stability scores of its candidates, a view of this catalog: the pipeline's report boxes the normalised expression of the top 25 genes per section instead. Section 1 holds the most expressed genes, and the chart answers how stable genes are at each level of expression.
    How to read: lower scores are more stable. Sections whose box sits lower offer better reference genes, and a wide box means the choice within that section matters.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median stability score of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of nf-core/stableexpression.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/stableexpression/blob/1.1.0/docs/output.md
  visu_type: box
  dict_kwargs:
    x: section
    y: stability_score
    color: section
    labels:
      section: Expression section
      stability_score: Stability score
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: stability_score

- component: interactive
  title: Expression section
  description: Keeps only the candidates of the chosen sections, to look for a reference gene at a given
    expression level.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: section

- component: interactive
  title: Expression level
  description: Keeps only candidates in the chosen expression level, from very high to very low.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: expression_level

- component: interactive
  title: Stability score
  description: Keeps only candidates whose stability score falls in the chosen range. Lower scores are more
    stable.
  interactive_type: RangeSlider
  column_name: stability_score

- component: table
  id: candidate_table
  title: Candidate genes table
  description: |-
    Each row is a candidate gene with its stability score, ranks, the four measures behind the score, its expression level and the platforms that measured it. It answers which genes to take forward as references and lets a row selection open the gene's record.
    How to read: sort by stability score or by section rank, and read the measured share beside it before trusting a low score.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: gene_id

- component: advanced_viz
  id: expression_plane
  title: Variation against mean expression
  description: |-
    Each point is a gene of the merged matrix: its mean normalised expression on the horizontal axis and its coefficient of variation on the vertical axis, coloured by whether it was shortlisted as a candidate. It answers where the stable genes sit relative to the rest.
    How to read: stable reference genes sit low, with little variation at their expression level. Candidates are picked from the lower edge of each expression section, so a gene far above that edge is not a good reference.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median coefficient of variation of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of nf-core/stableexpression, which defines none. Candidates are the lowest-variation genes of each section.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/stableexpression/blob/1.1.0/README.md
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Mean normalised expression
    y_title: Coefficient of variation
    top_n_labels: 10
    reference_line: horizontal
    reference_stat: median
  roles:
    x: mean
    y: cv
    label: gene_name
    color: candidate

- component: card
  id: gene_count
  title: Genes in the merged matrix
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of genes in the merged matrix, and the ring splits them into candidates and other genes. It answers how many genes were scored out of all those measured.
    How to read: candidates are a small shortlist per section, so a small share is expected. A matrix with few genes means strict ID mapping or occurrence filters removed many.
  column: gene_id
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: candidate
  caption: genes, candidate or not
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: gene_measured_share
  title: Share of samples measuring a gene
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median share of samples in which a gene was measured, and the histogram shows how it varies between genes. It answers how complete the merged matrix is.
    How to read: genes measured in few samples, usually from a single platform, carry weaker statistics. A histogram piled to the right is a complete matrix.
  column: measured_share
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: share measured, per gene

- component: card
  id: level_composition
  title: Genes by expression level
  description: |-
    Each unit is one gene and the bar shows the share of genes in each expression level, from very high to very low. It answers how the genes are spread over the expression range.
    How to read: the five levels are percentile bands of expression, so a heavily skewed split means the dataset mix favours some levels over others.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/stableexpression/blob/1.1.0/docs/output.md
  column: gene_id
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: expression_level
  caption: genes, by expression level

- component: figure
  id: cv_by_section
  title: Variation by expression section
  description: |-
    Each box is the distribution of the coefficient of variation of the genes in one expression section, split into candidates and other genes. It answers whether candidates are really the least variable genes of their section.
    How to read: the candidate box should sit below the other genes in every section. A section where it does not has few stable genes to choose from.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median coefficient of variation of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of nf-core/stableexpression.
  visu_type: box
  dict_kwargs:
    x: section
    y: cv
    color: candidate
    labels:
      section: Expression section
      cv: Coefficient of variation
      candidate: Candidate
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: cv

- component: figure
  id: source_ids_hist
  title: Source IDs per gene
  description: |-
    Each bar counts genes by how many source IDs (probes or transcripts) map onto them, coloured by the platforms that measured the gene. It answers how much the ID collapsing merged measurements.
    How to read: most genes should map from one or a few IDs. A long tail of many IDs per gene is typical of microarrays with several probes per gene.
  visu_type: histogram
  dict_kwargs:
    x: source_ids
    color: platforms
    labels:
      source_ids: Source IDs per gene
      platforms: Platforms

- component: interactive
  title: Expression level
  description: Keeps only genes in the chosen expression levels.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: expression_level

- component: interactive
  title: Platforms
  description: 'Keeps only genes measured by the chosen platform combination: RNA-seq only, microarray only
    or both.'
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: platforms

- component: table
  title: Gene statistics table
  description: |-
    Each row is a gene of the merged matrix with its mean, median, spread, coefficients of variation, measured share, expression level and per-platform statistics. It answers how any gene behaves across the datasets and lets a row selection filter the other tiles.
    How to read: sort by coefficient of variation to find the least variable genes, then check the measured share and the platforms.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: gene_id

- component: card
  id: id_fates
  title: Fate of gene IDs
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of gene IDs the datasets came with, and the bar splits them by fate: kept, collapsed, dropped as rare, or not mapped. It answers how much of the source identifiers reach the merged matrix.
    How to read: a large kept share is healthy. A large not-mapped share means the datasets use identifiers the mapping service does not know, and a large rare share means genes seen in too few datasets were removed.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/stableexpression/blob/1.1.0/docs/output.md
  column: gene_ids
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: fate
  caption: gene IDs, by fate

- component: figure
  id: id_fate_bars
  title: Gene ID fate per dataset
  description: |-
    Each bar is a dataset and its segments are the share of its gene IDs in each fate: kept, collapsed, rare or not mapped. It answers which datasets map well and which lose their genes.
    How to read: bars mostly kept are well mapped. A bar mostly not mapped is a dataset the pipeline could not use, so check its platform and identifier type.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/stableexpression/blob/1.1.0/docs/output.md
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: dataset
    y: share
    color: fate
    labels:
      dataset: Dataset
      share: Share of gene IDs
      fate: Fate

- component: figure
  id: id_fate_by_platform
  title: Gene ID fate by platform
  description: |-
    Each bar adds up the gene IDs of every dataset on one platform, split by fate. It answers whether microarray and RNA-seq datasets lose genes in the same way.
    How to read: microarray probes usually collapse onto fewer genes, while RNA-seq identifiers are closer to genes already. A platform with many unmapped IDs points to an identifier scheme the mapping does not cover.
  visu_type: histogram
  dict_kwargs:
    x: platform
    y: gene_ids
    color: fate
    histfunc: sum
    labels:
      platform: Platform
      gene_ids: Gene IDs
      fate: Fate

- component: interactive
  title: Fate
  description: Keeps only the chosen fates, for example the IDs that were not mapped.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: fate

- component: table
  title: Gene ID mapping table
  description: |-
    Each row is a dataset and a fate, with the number of gene IDs and their share of the dataset. It answers exactly how many IDs each dataset lost and why.
    How to read: sort by gene IDs within a fate to find the datasets that lose most, then check their outcome in the dataset summary.

- component: figure
  id: components_by_section
  title: What drives the score in each section
  description: |-
    Each bar is an expression section and its segments are the mean weighted part of each measure in the stability score: Normfinder, geNorm M, the coefficient of variation, the robust coefficient and the missing-value penalty. It answers which measure drives the score of each section.
    How to read: the height is the section's mean score, where lower is more stable. A large penalty segment means genes were missing from many samples, and a large segment for one measure means that measure separates the genes most.
    Lines and annotations: none are drawn. The weights of the four measures are a run parameter, equal by default.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/stableexpression/blob/1.1.0/nextflow_schema.json
  visu_type: histogram
  dict_kwargs:
    x: section
    y: contribution
    color: component
    histfunc: avg
    labels:
      section: Expression section
      contribution: Mean contribution to the score
      component: Part of the score

- component: interactive
  title: Part of the score
  description: Keeps only the chosen parts of the score, to compare one measure across sections.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: component

- component: table
  title: Score parts table
  description: |-
    Each row is one part of one candidate gene's stability score, with the normalised measure and its weighted contribution. It answers how a gene's score adds up.
    How to read: a gene's parts sum to its stability score, so sort by contribution to see which measure holds a gene back.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: stability_ranking
  title: Most stable genes and their spread
  description: |-
    Each row is one of the best-ranked candidate genes of an expression section, coloured by section: a box of its normalised expression over the samples that measured it, beside the stability score that ranked it. It answers which genes are the best reference candidates and how steady their expression is.
    How to read: a good reference has a short box and a low score. A long box or a long whisker means the gene varies between samples or datasets, whatever its rank. Compare genes of the same section, since sections differ in level.
    Lines and annotations: the box spans the first to the third quartile with the median inside, and whiskers reach the furthest values within 1.5 times the interquartile range (Tukey's rule, computed by this catalog's recipe). The pipeline's report also draws boxes of the normalised expression of the top 25 genes per section.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/stableexpression/blob/1.1.0/docs/output.md
  kind: ranked_distribution
  config:
    score_label: Stability score (lower is more stable)
    value_label: Normalised expression
  roles:
    feature_id: gene_id
    score: stability_score
    rank: section_rank
    label: gene_name
    group: section
    q1: q1
    median: median
    q3: q3
    lower: lower
    upper: upper
    mean: mean

- component: card
  id: ranked_gene_count
  title: Top genes drawn
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct top-ranked genes, and the bar splits them by expression level. It answers which part of the expression range the best candidates come from.
    How to read: top candidates are taken per section, so each level should be represented. A level with none has no stable genes in this run.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/stableexpression/blob/1.1.0/docs/output.md
  column: gene_id
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: expression_level
  caption: genes, by expression level

- component: card
  id: ranked_measured_share
  title: Share of samples measuring a gene
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median share of samples in which a top gene was measured, and the histogram shows its spread. It answers how much evidence stands behind the box statistics.
    How to read: genes measured in only a few samples are less reliable references, even with a low score. Prefer genes near the right edge.
  column: measured_share
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: share measured, per gene

- component: figure
  id: ranked_iqr_figure
  title: Stability score against median expression
  description: |-
    Each point is a top-ranked gene: its median normalised expression against its stability score, coloured by section. It answers whether the most stable genes are also the most highly expressed.
    How to read: lower scores are more stable. Points low at their level are good reference candidates, and a trend with expression means the score depends on level.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median stability score of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of the pipeline.
  visu_type: scatter
  dict_kwargs:
    x: median
    y: stability_score
    color: section
    labels:
      median: Median normalised expression
      stability_score: Stability score
      section: Expression section
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: stability_score
    label: Median stability score

- component: interactive
  title: Expression section
  description: Keeps only the genes of the chosen sections.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: section

- component: interactive
  title: Stability score
  description: Keeps only genes whose stability score falls in the chosen range. Lower scores are more stable.
  interactive_type: RangeSlider
  column_name: stability_score

- component: table
  title: Top genes table
  description: |-
    Each row is a top-ranked candidate gene with its stability score, ranks, box statistics and measured share. It answers the exact numbers behind the box view and lets a row selection filter the other tiles.
    How to read: sort by section rank to see the best gene of each section, and read the quartiles for the spread of its expression.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: gene_id

- component: advanced_viz
  id: stability_violins
  title: Most stable genes across samples
  description: |-
    Each row is one of the top candidate genes of an expression section, coloured by section: the distribution of its normalised expression over the samples in view, beside its stability score. It answers how steady a gene's expression is across datasets, and recomputes when you filter samples.
    How to read: a narrow distribution with a low score marks a reliable reference gene. A wide or multi-peaked shape means expression differs between datasets or platforms, so filter by dataset to see which.
    Lines and annotations: none are drawn. The score ranks the genes within their section and has no published cut-off.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/stableexpression/blob/1.1.0/docs/output.md
  kind: ranked_distribution
  config:
    distribution: violin
    score_label: Stability score (lower is more stable)
    value_label: Normalised expression
  roles:
    feature_id: gene_id
    score: stability_score
    rank: section_rank
    label: gene_name
    group: section
    value: value

- component: figure
  id: value_box
  title: Expression of the top genes
  description: |-
    Each box is a top candidate gene and summarises its normalised expression over the samples in view, coloured by section. It answers how the best candidates compare in level and spread.
    How to read: boxes at the same height with a short spread are interchangeable references. A box that moves when you filter by dataset depends on the dataset and is a weaker reference.
  visu_type: box
  dict_kwargs:
    x: gene_name
    y: value
    color: section
    labels:
      gene_name: Gene
      value: Normalised expression
      section: Expression section

- component: card
  title: Samples in view
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct samples behind the gene values, and the bars rank the datasets that contribute most. It answers how large the evidence is and whether one dataset dominates.
    How to read: if one dataset holds most samples, the stability of the top genes mostly reflects that dataset. Filter by dataset to test this.
  column: sample
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: dataset
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: samples, the largest datasets

- component: interactive
  title: Dataset
  description: Keeps only the samples of the chosen datasets, so each gene's distribution is recomputed
    from them.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: dataset
